title: Seventeenth-century German watch
fact: The collection identifies gilded metal and a seventeenth-century date.
limit: The photographed exterior gives no interval between the ticks of the movement.
alt: Small oval gold-coloured case with an upper ring.

title: Ray and Montague watch
material: gold, silver, pearls, diamonds, and enamel
fact: The Cleveland record dates the watch to 1813 and credits John Ray, James Montague and Just and Son in different roles.
limit: Its case decoration and documented makers give useful identity. A new running record is needed to check the rate.
alt: Circular case with a dark jewelled border and small winding ring.

title: Engraved Egg Watch
fact: Cleveland credits Denis Martinot as designer and attributes the decoration to Theodor de Bry. The catalogue lists silver, steel and rock crystal.
limit: An engraving can link a design to a source. It leaves the case’s running rate to its movement.
alt: Oval watch with an elaborate repeating design and a loop at the top.

title: Marchand’s enamelled watch
material: enameled case mounted in engraved gilded metal
fact: The catalogue names Marchand and identifies the enamelled case mounted in engraved gilded metal.
limit: The case and dial show how the object is presented. Their appearance leaves its regularity open.
alt: Open watch with circular enamel decoration and a separate dial.

title: Swiss chatelaine watch
fact: The museum names metal and enamel and dates the chatelaine watch to the mid-nineteenth century.
limit: The pendant view shows how a dial can be carried. It gives no record of a reading taken while it moved.
alt: An ornate hanging arrangement holds a small round dial at its lowest point.

title: Italian watch case
fact: This catalogue entry is for a watch case in crystal, gilt metal and enamel.
limit: A case is evidence for a cover and its material. The movement needs its own record.
alt: Ring-shaped watch case with a dark translucent centre.

title: Jewelled American pendant watch
dimensions: Overall: 6 x 2.5 x 2 cm (2 3/8 x 1 x 13/16 in.)
fact: The museum records a pendant watch in gold and platinum with stones and a pearl.
limit: Its material and form can guide a display. The image does not measure its running pace.
alt: An ornate pendant with a pearl link and a round white form set with stones.

title: Wigström nephrite clock
feature: small face on the stone case
fact: The record names Henrik Wigström and the House of Fabergé and identifies the green case as nephrite.
limit: The stone helps identify the worked case for the catalogue. Its appearance does not give a rate.
alt: A rectangular dark green clock with a small dial and light corner marks.

title: Kremlin Tower Clock
fact: The House of Fabergé catalogue piece is a clock styled as the Kremlin tower, made with rhodonite and other materials.
limit: The shaped case depicts a tower. This accession gives no direct timing record from the tower itself.
alt: A tall pink model tower has green accents and a circular dial.

title: James Cox’s cabinet clock
fact: The museum credits James Cox and lists gold, agate, an enamel dial and glass.
limit: The catalogue identifies a dial within the cabinet. A still image preserves one reading position.
alt: Square cabinet clock with paired decorative panels below the face.

title: Butterfield-type silver sundial

people.name: Michael Butterfield
people.role: Instrument maker for whom the dial style is named

fact: The museum describes an adjustable gnomon, which casts a shadow on the dial. It connects the style’s name to the English instrument maker Butterfield, who worked in Paris.
limit: The shadow depends on the light and the instrument’s position. A missing shadow leaves a reading open.
alt: An octagonal engraved dial carries a small hinged fin.

title: Tiffany & Co. tall clock
material: mahogany, teak with dial faces of gilded and patinated metal, glass
fact: Cleveland lists Tiffany & Co., mahogany and teak, and dial surfaces in gilded and patinated metal.
limit: The case records material and scale. More than one time reading is needed for a rate.
alt: A tall carved wooden case with a dial across the upper front.

title: Boulle and Martinot clock
material: tortoise shell and brass inlay, gilt bronze
fact: The museum names the cabinetmaker André-Charles Boulle and clockmaker Balthazar Martinot II.
limit: The two attributions are separate contributions. The case pattern cannot measure how the movement runs.
alt: A tall dark clock with gilt figures and inlay around its face.

title: Paris mantel clock
fact: The museum records marble, gilt bronze and glass for this mantel clock, dated about 1780–90.
limit: The collection photograph preserves a presentation of the dial and case. It has no sequence for working out elapsed time.
alt: A light dial sits above two dark columns and between gilt figures.

title: Latz and Stollewerck tall-case clock
material: boulle marquetry with gilt bronze mounts
fact: The collection dates the clock to 1744 and credits Jean-Pierre Latz and Stollewerck in separate work roles.
limit: The maker record and the readout identify the instrument. A timed comparison is needed to establish an observed pace.
alt: A narrow ornate standing case carries a large dial high on the front.

title: Baumgartinger clock
fact: Cleveland names Baumgartinger and lists carved and gilded wood with faience.
limit: The carved surround and maker line identify this case. A rate needs readings separated by an observed interval.
alt: A gilt sculpted clock stand frames a circular dial.

title: Gilt French wall clock
fact: The catalogue places the gilt bronze wall clock in France around 1750–60.
limit: The front can face a public space while its inner rate remains separate evidence.
alt: An elongated gilded clock case has an openwork surround around the face.

title: Tiffany and Lenzkirch mantel clock
place: American and German firms named separately
fact: The collection credits Tiffany & Co. and the Lenzkirch Clock Factory and gives the date 1901.
limit: The maker records belong to their respective contributions. A still dial view cannot check later accuracy.
alt: A curved wooden case has an upper dial and a small lower opening.

title: Japanese wall clock 00.12.10
fact: The Met records this Japanese wall clock with accession 00.12.10 and a nineteenth-century date.
limit: The collection view shows a dial and long case. How a particular owner read them needs another record.
alt: Long narrow wall clock with a small rectangular top and a marked vertical strip.

title: Japanese wall clock 00.12.11
fact: The Met catalogues this as a separate nineteenth-century Japanese wall clock, accession 00.12.11.
limit: The similar cases have two accessions. One cannot establish what the other display showed at a given time.
alt: A narrow dark wooden case has an upper circular feature above a single long door.

title: Japanese astronomical clock
fact: The Met calls accession 00.12.19 an astronomical clock and assigns an eighteenth- to nineteenth-century date.
limit: The large dial shows the form of a display. Its photograph gives no successive observations for running pace.
alt: Black case with a wide circular pale dial marked in rings.

title: Egyptian water clock with a baboon
catalogueTitle: Water Clock Decorated with a Baboon
fact: The Met identifies the object as a water clock with a baboon and dates it to 664–30 BCE.
limit: The intact-looking form offers an object study. The trial’s water levels and elapsed marks are invented.
alt: Pale small rectangular object with a recessed front and sculpted animal.

title: Egyptian Shadow Clock
fact: The Met gives a Ptolemaic-period range of 305–30 BCE and identifies this object as a shadow clock.
limit: A shadow clock’s reading needs a case with illumination and position. Its stone can still be studied without a shadow.
alt: A brown stepped object slopes up towards a broad standing end.

title: Musical Clock with Spinet and Organ
catalogueTitle: Musical Clock with Spinet and Organ
material: Ebony, gliding, brass, silver gilt, gilt brass, iron, various wood and metals, wire, parchment and leather
fact: The Met names Veit Langenbucher and Samuel Bidermann in its record for this musical clock with a spinet and organ.
limit: A caption can identify its music apparatus. Its original sound and timing are separate tests.
alt: A dark tall case shows arched compartments and small gold-coloured figures.

title: Bockeltz astronomical clock-watch
catalogueTitle: Clock watch with astronomical dial and sundial
material: Case: gilded brass; Dial: gilded brass, silver, and copper; Movement: gilded brass, partly blued steel, and silver
dimensions: Overall: 3 1/2 × 2 7/16 × 2 5/16 in. (8.9 × 6.2 × 5.9 cm); Width of back plate: 2 1/8 in. (5.4 cm)
fact: The Met credits Jan Jansen Bockeltz and identifies both an astronomical dial and a sundial.
limit: Two readouts in one object can use different references. One captured reading does not calibrate both.
alt: Small gold clock-watch lies open with a gold lid and a circular face.

title: Forfaict clock-watch with alarm
material: Movement: gilded breass and steel, partly blued; case and dial: brass, silvered brass, silver; hand: steel
fact: The Met credits Nicolas Forfaict and catalogues an alarm alongside the calendar.
limit: A cue and calendar give different readings. An alarm heard once gives no evidence of the later pace.
alt: Gold open watch with a light face and an ornamented edge.

title: Augsburg astronomical table clock
material: Case: gilded brass and gilded copper; Dials: gilded brass and silver; Movement: brass, gilded brass, and steel
fact: The Met dates this German astronomical table clock to the second quarter of the seventeenth century.
limit: The astronomical face identifies a display type. A still position cannot give its changes over time.
alt: Gold-coloured clock tower with a circular central dial and a pointed crown.

title: David Beringer’s portable cube sundial
fact: The Met credits David Beringer and identifies this as a portable cube sundial.
limit: A shadow shown on one face depends on how the cube is placed and lit.
alt: Pale cube with a pointed top fin on a dark wooden stand.

title: Charles Bloud’s diptych sundial
fact: The Met credits Charles Bloud and dates the portable diptych sundial to about 1666–80.
limit: The open leaves show the instrument’s shape. Its reading depends on where and how the piece is used.
alt: Open rectangular sundial with a marked circle on each leaf.

title: Tompion repeater and Northcott case
fact: The Met identifies both Thomas Tompion and John Northcott in the repeater watch and case record.
limit: The case and work are distinct contributions. The collection view supplies no historical sound sample.
alt: A round watch with a complex light face and a dark narrow frame.

title: Johann Wutky repeater watch
material: Case: pierced and incised brass, with silver dial; Movement: brass; steel, partly blued; and silver
fact: The Met credits Johann Wutky in its record for this repeater watch, dated about 1675–80.
limit: The image shows the closed ornament. Sounding the historical watch would require a separate recorded observation.
alt: Gold round watch with an ornate perforated-looking cover and a ring.

title: Bordier Frères calendar watch
material: Case: varicolored gold, partly enameled; Dial: white enamel; Movement: brass and steel
dimensions:
Diameter (case): 1 1/2 in. (3.8 cm);
Diameter (back plate): 1 3/16 in. (3 cm)
fact: The Met identifies the firm of Bordier Frères and dates its calendar watch to about 1780–90.
limit: The catalogue records a calendar display. The decorative side leaves its calendar position hidden.
alt: An oval red and gold case surrounds a portrait and has a loop above.

title: Godemar musical repeater
fact: The Met’s record names Godemar of Geneva and describes the object as a musical repeater watch.
limit: Its outward portrait and musical capability use different records. The original tune is not recovered here.
alt: A watch case has an oval pale portrait inside a dark surround.

title: Delaunoy oscillating clock
catalogueTitle: Clock in the form of an oscillating pendulum (pendule oscillante)
fact: The Met names Delaunoy and describes the case as a clock in the form of an oscillating pendulum.
limit: The appearance of a pendulum shape does not give the repeated intervals of the clock in operation.
alt: A pale clock face hangs beneath a narrow curving tall frame.

title: Aaron Willard Jr. banjo clock
material: Mahogany, gilt gesso, eglomise tablets, white pine, tulip poplar
fact: The Met credits Aaron Willard Jr. and dates this banjo clock to about 1825.
limit: The shape identifies a kind of case. Testing its pace would need separated readings.
alt: A narrow tall case links a round upper dial to a rectangular lower box.

title: Boston Clock Company carriage clock
fact: The Met credits the Boston Clock Company and dates this carriage clock to about 1890.
limit: Portability gives a setting for a comparison. The archival record does not quantify its rate in motion.
alt: A compact rectangular clock has an upper handle and a front dial.

title: Forestville acorn clock
feature: dial in a shaped shelf case
fact: The Met credits the Forestville Manufacturing Company and dates the clock to 1847–50.
limit: The collection photograph records its form. A schedule needs a second time observation as well.
alt: Dark brown shelf clock with a round upper section and a broad curved base.

title: Isaac Johnson’s sundial
fact: The museum credits Isaac Johnson and gives the date 1731.
limit: Its engraved scale survives as evidence. A prediction from a shadow still needs a specific position and light.
alt: Flat brass plate with engraved radiating lines and characters.

title: Goldsmith Chandlee sundial
fact: The Met credits Goldsmith Chandlee and dates the sundial to about 1800.
limit: A photograph at one orientation presents the scale. It gives no reading at another hour by itself.
alt: Square plate with a circular scale and a dark upright pointer.

title: Lépine clock with Arabic calendar inscriptions
catalogueTitle: Clock with perpetual calendar and moon cycle inscribed in Arabic
place: French maker and Arabic inscription, separately recorded
fact: The museum names Jean Antoine Lépine and catalogues a perpetual calendar and moon cycle with Arabic inscriptions.
limit: The maker’s attribution and the language on the instrument are different pieces of evidence. Neither identifies every person who read it.
alt: Gilded clock with three circular displays and an ornamented crest.
